text:
Nora: Quick questionwe're debating publish patterns for the JS SDK. Do we do a single package + conditional exports, or keep separate @redwood/sdk and @redwood/sdk-edge packages? Edge compatibility + types resolution are the sticking points. Thoughts?

Jules: Single package + exports map is nicer for discoverability (one npm name). Splitting forces users to learn two names and complicates versioning. But packaging becomes fiddly (per-subpath types, extra d.ts files).

Ravi: Agreed on single package. Practical plan: build three artifacts -> dist/index.cjs, dist/index.mjs, dist/edge.mjs. Use "exports" to point: import -> .mjs, require -> .cjs, ./edge -> edge.mjs. Then provide declarations in dist/*.d.ts and set "types" to dist/index.d.ts.

Nora: TS editor resolution is the worry. People import `@redwood-inference/sdk/runtime` in examples and some editors can't find runtime types unless we expose that subpath in exports and give a runtime.d.ts. Do we want to enumerate every public subpath? That's more work.

Jules: There's also typesVersions trickery if we want path mapping for older TS. Another path: ship a single comprehensive index.d.ts that re-exports everything from subpath declarations (index.d.ts -> export * from './runtime';). That way editors resolving top-level types get coverage for subpaths used by consumers. Not perfect for deep imports like `@redwood-inference/sdk/runtime/internal` but we shouldn't encourage deep/internal imports.

Ravi: On the edge side, Cloudflare/Worker import will blow up if package.json's main points at a CJS file or if published tarball omits .mjs files. We had a customer report: "Unexpected token 'export'" when importing. CI should pack and test the tarball in a minimal worker runtime (miniflare) and in Node ESM.

Nora: Example exports we considered: 
```
"exports": {
  ".": {"import": "./dist/index.mjs","require": "./dist/index.cjs"},
  "./edge": {"import": "./dist/edge.mjs"},
  "./runtime": {"import": "./dist/runtime.mjs","require": "./dist/runtime.cjs"},
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```
plus "types": "./dist/index.d.ts". Does that look sane?

Jules: Yes. Also add "files" globs to include *.mjs and *.d.ts. pkg-bot historically flagged missing d.ts in a subpath.

pkg-bot: publish check failed: missing artifact dist/runtime.mjs; missing types for export ./runtime -> dist/runtime.d.ts. See CI artifact: https://ci.redwood.dev/pack/991

Ravi: Ok that's actionable. I'll update the rollup/tsc output to emit runtime.mjs and runtime.d.ts. For bundlers, ensure we don't set "type": "module" globally to avoid breaking require consumers; conditional exports will route correctly.

Nora: Also we should update the sample app in examples/ to import from top-level and from ./edge and verify those imports work when installed from the published tarball. The common onboarding mess is examples that import internal paths which break on published package.

Jules: Good call. Add a smoke test step: npm pack -> tarball -> npm install in example -> run tests (node cjs import, node esm import, miniflare edge import). If any step fails, fail the publish.

Ravi: One more nuance: bundlers sometimes prefer .js extension for ESM. Maybe emit index.mjs and a copy index.js that is identical. Slightly ugly but improves compatibility with older toolchains.

Nora: Checklist for PR:
- build cjs + mjs + edge artifacts and matching .d.ts files
- export map with explicit subpaths we support
- include dist/*.mjs, dist/*.cjs, dist/*.d.ts in files
- CI smoke: pack + install + node-cjs + node-esm + miniflare worker
- update examples and README import recommendations
- run a dry-run publish and notify pkg-bot

Jules: I'll draft README snippets showing preferred imports and call out "do not import from /internal".

Ravi: I'll open the packaging PR with tests. Tagging @pkg-bot to re-run pack checks once ready.

pkg-bot: ack. once PR opened will run pack checks automatically.

Nora: Great, thanks. Let's avoid splitting packages unless we absolutely need to. Single package + careful exports + good CI seems like the best DX tradeoff. :rocket:
